title: BenchX target description
description: What a target provider hands the workbench about one prepared target (docs/design/system-decomposition.md §3.4). The same document arrives three ways: on a provider's stdout, as a sidecar file .benchx-target.json in a build directory, or assembled by the workbench from the user's own input. The workbench copies target, build, how_built, activation and shell into the work order's target, and labels into the order's labels. Nothing else in a work order comes from a provider.
$comment: target and build are $refs into urn:benchx:schema:work-order:0.1.0, so the two cannot drift; a validator must register that schema (and the measurement-result schema it refs) together with this one. Paths are absolute because the workbench and the runner may not share a working directory; the schema enforces this for working_tree and build targets. how_built, activation, shell and provider are $refs into the work-order schema's provenanceText, so a description copies into an order unchanged. how_built and activation are declared provenance text (benchmark-environments.md §3.2): recorded as given, never executed and never checked against anything. The user activates the environment before invoking benchx, and the runner records what it inherited. Absent, null, empty, or whitespace-only means not declared. Neither text enters identity. Both are copied verbatim into results, which may be promoted to a shared store, so neither may hold secrets.

build.description: The declared configuration of the prebuilt target, for facts the runner cannot read from it. The work-order build object, unchanged.

labels.description: Caller labels for selecting sides of a comparison, copied to the order's labels. Never enter identity.
